title: Latticeway: simplify workspace lanes and affordance clarity probe
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Exploratory design probe to simplify the Console's primary vertical lanes (workspaces, projects, routes) into a grid-first information architecture called 'Latticeway'. Goal: reduce cognitive load for cross-workspace workflows (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) while surfacing rollback + canary controls and cost lenses with minimal clicks.
background: Current sidebar and workspace switch patterns accumulate deep nested routes and duplicate entry points for dashboards and rollout controls. Product and engineering have surface-level telemetry showing jump rates between workspace context and rollout config pages; users report losing context when switching workspaces while viewing cost breakdowns. This probe synthesizes a tile/grid navigation metaphor to preserve context and make affordances (rollout state, active cost lens, SLO health) visible without deep navigation.
goals: Reduce path length to common tasks (open rollout, view cost breakdown, open model route) to 1-2 clicks
Expose rollout status and canary controls inline on workspace tiles
Make cost-lens toggles (unit cost, latency, token breakdown) discoverable in the nav surface
Preserve keyboard-first navigation and ARIA semantics for accessibility
Produce a high-fidelity prototype for usability testing and engineering handoff
non_goals: Renovate every console screen in this ticket
Ship changes to Dedicated control plane in the first cut
deliverables: Annotated IA spec with route mapping and fallback flows
Engineering handoff kit with component list and telemetry events
design_decisions: Adopt a 3-column grid for workspace tiles on desktop; collapse to stacked cards on mobile
Tile header contains persistent micro-status (SLO icon, cost delta, rollout badge)
Primary tile actions: 'Open', 'Rollout controls', 'Cost lens' — surfaced via hover affordance and keyboard focus
Keep legacy sidebar as a condensed 'utility rail' for deep links and quick actions during rollout migration
Expose experimental 'context pin' that preserves dashboard state across workspace switches
tradeoffs_and_risks: Grid-first IA increases visual density; must be mitigated with clear hierarchy and progressive reveal
Adding micro-status badges may create noise for power users; provide a settings toggle to compress indicators
Changing workspace switching semantics risks breaking existing session-shortcuts and third-party bookmarks; plan deprecation window and redirect rules
acceptance_criteria: Prototype clickable end-to-end flows for: open dashboard -> switch workspace with context pin -> open rollout panel
Usability test with 6 internal engineers and 6 external beta customers with 80% task success on key flows
Annotated IA doc mapping old routes to new grid routes and preserving query params for dashboard state
Engineering PR with skeleton components and telemetry events approved by infra/eng leads
accessibility_notes: Tile actions must be reachable with arrow/tab navigation; focus ring must be visible
Micro-status icons include text alternatives; rollup table available for screen readers
Color choices validated for 4.5:1 contrast for critical badges
tasks: Design: finalize grid breakpoints and compact tile layout
Research: run moderated usability sessions (2 rounds)
PM: align rollout migration plan with infra and docs
Engineering: build skeleton components and flag for gradual rollout
qa_notes: Verify keyboard flow for tile focus/activation
Check preservation of dashboard query params when context pin is used
Validate telemetry events are emitted for tile action clicks and workspace switches
